html:
Riga was founded in 1201 by Albert, a German bishop from Bremen, near the mouth of the Daugava river on the Baltic coast. It became the largest city and port of the Baltic lands and is today the capital of Latvia.

German merchants had already traded with the local Livs there for some decades. Albert came with crusaders to convert the pagan peoples of Livonia by force, part of the Northern Crusades. He moved his see to Riga and in 1202 founded the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, a military order later joined to the Teutonic Order.

Riga grew rich on the river trade with Russia, sending furs, wax, flax and timber west. It joined the Hanseatic League in 1282, and its mostly German merchants ran the city for centuries. Bishops, knights and citizens often fought over who controlled it. Riga later passed to Poland-Lithuania, then Sweden, and in 1710 Russia, but its German elite lasted into the 20th century.
